title: Ancient Egyptians may have built a massive dam near the Red Pyramid | New Scientist
description: Large structures near the Red Pyramid may be the remnants of a major dam, suggesting that the Egyptians used water to help power their construction projects
author: Taylor Mitchell Brown

title: X rocket crashes into moon at 8700 kilometres per hour | New Scientist
description: A rocket launched last year is thought to have smashed into the lunar surface this morning, creating the moon's newest crater
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: Most people prefer AI-written stories – and can't tell when they are made by humans | New Scientist
description: People appear to prefer short stories created by AI over those written by humans. They are also no better than chance at telling which is which
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: Should you stop using preventive flea treatments on your pets? | New Scientist
description: It has been assumed for decades that tick and flea treatments for pets pose no threat to wildlife or people, but there’s growing evidence that we have got it wrong
author: Michael Le Page

title: Darwin proved right about gnat-trapping carnivorous plant | New Scientist
description: Botanists have finally proved what Charles Darwin was unable to nail down – that a genus of plants known to catch insects also digests them, suggesting the extent of plant carnivory has been underestimated
author: James Woodford

title: Canadian wildfires are reducing solar power generation in Europe | New Scientist
description: Lost solar power due to smoke blocking the sun cost Europe and North America nearly $2 billion in 2023 alone
author: Michael Le Page
